conventions.convention: The domain is a bounded connected planar Lipschitz polygon and a W^{1,2} extension domain. Positive-length closed Dirichlet and contact segments are disjoint and lie strictly inside straight sides. Traces use fixed C1 interior collars; V has the full H1 norm.
The fixed unit normal is oriented so positive normal displacement opens the gap. Feasibility is T_C v·n ≥ ψ, with continuous ψ ≤ 0; the VI is a(u,v−u) ≥ F(v−u).
The shear modulus is constant and positive; the Lamé parameter is finite and nonnegative. The form uses 2μ ε(u):ε(v) + λ div(u) div(v).
Meshes are matching, boundary-conforming, shape-regular affine triangles resolving both segments. Nodal conformity requires ψ to be convex in contact arclength as well as continuous and nonpositive.

The mortar cone is coefficientwise nonnegative; its functions need not be pointwise nonnegative. Pairing uses exact edge integration on a matching partition. Uniform inf-sup stability is stated in L2 norms on the multiplier and scalar trace spaces.
AC is assumed in the partial-trace geometry and inherited Sobolev interfaces; Countable Choice is used by the divergence lift and Stampacchia branches.

load_bearing.statement: There is c_K > 0, depending on Ω and Γ_D, such that ‖v‖_{H1(Ω)} ≤ c_K ‖ε(v)‖_{L2(Ω)} for every v ∈ V, under the geometry of def-signorini-partial-trace-space.
The maps T_D and T_C from H1(Ω;R2) to the respective L2 boundary-segment spaces are bounded and linear, and V = ker T_D is Hilbert with the inherited H1 inner product.

Under def-signorini-nodal-p1-contact-scheme, K_h is nonempty, closed and convex in finite-dimensional V_h, and K_h ⊆ K. For v ∈ K ∩ H2(Ω;R2) ∩ C(Ω̄;R2), its global P1 nodal interpolant belongs to V_h and K_h.
For every bounded linear load F on V there is exactly one contact VI solution u ∈ K. With α = 2μ/c_K², solutions for two loads satisfy α‖u_1−u_2‖_V ≤ ‖F_1−F_2‖_{V*}.
The map B:V_h → R^{N+1}, B_i(v_h) = v_h(a_i)·n, is onto; each contact coordinate has a test function w_i with B_j(w_i) = δ_ij.
With d_i equal to the sum of incident contact-edge lengths, ∫χ_i φ_j = d_i δ_ij. The pair (Λ_h,W_h) has L2 trace-space inf-sup constant at least 1/√3, and its pairing is Σ_i d_i λ_i g_h(a_i).

concerns.concern: The Definition fixes closed segments Γ_D, Γ_C, then requires collar boundaries to contain them “as relatively open flat patches.” A positive-length closed segment cannot itself be relatively open in a C1 boundary: its endpoints have boundary neighborhoods extending beyond the segment. The intended geometry is clear if each closed segment is contained in a relatively open flat patch, or if only its relative interior is called the patch. Clarify this endpoint wording; subsequent trace arguments only require containment.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data against the contact definition. The supplier explicitly defines the strain and energy formulas for all H1 fields; the contact model specializes to constant μ and repeats those formulas on its partial-trace space. It does not transfer full-Dirichlet coercivity, well-posedness, or nearly incompressible stability. Partial-boundary Korn coercivity is proved locally.
